### 8–16s — CA07-DIAGRAM-1
Voiceover: 01 · GRAMMAR — What makes the image-world recognizable?. Trace light, distance, movement, lens position, setting, casting, color, sequencing, and refusal across a defined body of work. Describe patterns without claiming the house or photographer owns an abstract style.

Treatment: vertical reveal with source footer

Credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins

Rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

### 16–24s — CA07-DIAGRAM-2
Voiceover: 02 · AUTHOR — Who created the photograph?. Preserve photographer, assistants, digital technician, set, styling, model, hair, makeup, retouching, and commissioner records. Under U.S. guidance, do not assume a commission alone answers work-made-for-hire status.

Treatment: slow evidence push; no synthetic parallax

Credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins

Rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

### 24–32s — CA07-DIAGRAM-3
Voiceover: 03 · LICENSE — What may the house actually do?. Attach usage media, territory, term, exclusivity, crops, derivatives, credits, embargoes, archive copies, portfolio uses, and approval language. Route ownership and transfer questions to counsel with the executed agreement.

Treatment: vertical reveal with source footer

Credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins

Rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

### 32–40s — CA07-DIAGRAM-4
Voiceover: 04 · MEMORY — Whose archive preserves the house image?. Map negatives or RAW files, selects, contact sheets, captions, model releases, licenses, expiry, publication proofs, and preservation custody. Cultural memory may depend on a record the house does not own.

Treatment: slow evidence push; no synthetic parallax

Credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins

Rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
